style.vernacular: Greater Banjul (Kombos) is low-rise: one to two storey cement-block houses in cream, white, pale blue and ochre paint behind compound walls, shops and workshops with corrugated iron roofs, and a few three to five storey concrete blocks in Banjul and along Kairaba Avenue. Banjul island keeps Victorian and Edwardian colonial buildings with verandas and louvred shutters. Streets are sandy, with mango, neem, oil palm and silk-cotton trees giving shade.
style.ornament: Colonial verandas with timber posts and louvred shutters in Banjul; pierced concrete breeze-block screens and arched openings on mosques; Islamic green-and-white trim; painted shop-front signs and murals; thatched palm shelters at beach bars.
